title: Do pairwise interaction terms improve held-out AUROC on the synthetic set?
summary: This project asks whether explicit pairwise interaction terms help a simple classifier on a synthetic two-class set whose generator plants exactly one interaction. A logistic regression is fitted with and without all 28 pairwise products of the eight features, on ten generator seeds, and scored by held-out AUROC on split_b, the differences paired within a seed. Two controls frame the gain: a small multilayer network on the raw features, which asks whether a flexible model recovers the interaction without the products, and a null set generated with no interaction, on which the products should change nothing. The work is synthetic only and makes no claim about real data; it is a small, fully scripted test of whether the products carry the planted signal and nothing else.
question: On the toy generator's synthetic two-class set, does a logistic regression given all 28 pairwise products of x0..x7 reach a higher held-out AUROC on split_b than the same model without them, by at least +0.02 averaged over ten generator seeds, and does that gain survive a flexible model without products and vanish on a set with no planted interaction?

claims.text: Adding all 28 pairwise products to a logistic regression raises held-out AUROC on split_b by at least +0.02, mean over ten generator seeds, paired within a seed.
The products' gain is not matched by a small multilayer network on the raw features, so explicit products carry information a flexible model without them does not recover at this size.
The gain comes from the planted interaction: on a set generated with interaction 0 the products change held-out AUROC by less than 0.005.

anti_claims.text: No claim is made about real data: the set plants exactly one product, and the result is synthetic-only.
No product's coefficient is read as a discovery; if the gain appears on the null set, the method is fitting noise and C1 is withdrawn.

methods.name: logistic regression
methods.text: scikit-learn LogisticRegression with library defaults, installed in the project's own virtual environment (Q3), on the raw features, with and without the 28 pairwise products (Q4).

methods.name: small network
methods.text: scikit-learn MLPClassifier on the raw features, its settings tuned by 5-fold cross-validation inside split_a with the same grid on every seed.

methods.name: paired comparison
methods.text: Each seed generates a fresh 20000-row set, split_b its last quarter; each model is scored on split_b and differences are paired within a seed (Q5).

experiments.design: For generator seeds 0-9 at the default signal and interaction, fit the logistic regression with and without products on split_a and score both on split_b; report the mean and standard deviation of the paired difference.
experiments.success: mean paired auroc_gain >= 0.02 over the ten seeds

experiments.design: On the same ten sets, fit the small network on the raw features and score it on split_b; compare with the with-products logistic regression, paired within a seed.
experiments.success: the with-products logistic regression beats the network by a mean paired margin above zero
experiments.budget: up to 3 hours of CPU for the cross-validated grid

experiments.design: Repeat E1 on sets generated with interaction 0 for seeds 0-9.

baselines.text: logistic regression on the raw features, no products
small multilayer network on the raw features, no products
planted-only logistic regression (x2*x3 alone), an oracle reference, not a competitor

data.text: toy/make_synthetic.py at default signal 1.0 and interaction 0.6, seeds 0-9, 20000 rows each; split_a the first three quarters, split_b the last
the same generator at interaction 0, seeds 0-9 (the null control)

metrics.name: auroc
metrics.definition: area under the ROC curve of the model's scores on split_b

metrics.name: auroc_gain
metrics.definition: paired difference in split_b AUROC between the with-products model and its comparison, per seed, then the mean over seeds

success_criteria.text: C1 holds when E1's mean paired gain is at least +0.02 (the goal of GOAL.json).
C3 holds when E3's gain is under 0.005 in absolute value; otherwise C1 is withdrawn (A2).

budgets.notes: 4 hours of CPU wall clock in total (Q6); no GPU.

out_of_scope: a sweep of the generator's interaction strength beyond 0 and the default
product selection or any reading of which product matters

risks.text: The network's cross-validated grid overruns the 4-hour budget.
risks.mitigation: cap the grid at what fits 3 hours on the first seed, and keep that grid for every seed.

risks.text: The ceiling spread across seeds (0.7445-0.7511) is a third of the target gain.
risks.mitigation: pair every comparison within a seed and report the paired standard deviation.

seams.name: the set
seams.text: toy/make_synthetic.py writes one CSV per seed and interaction; every experiment reads only those files.

seams.name: the scores
seams.text: each fitted model writes predictions/<model>-<seed>.csv with a score per split_b row; toy/eval.py and toy/paired_gain.py read only those.
